Understanding the cost of tourism in Russia helps you build a realistic trip instead of relying on a vague general estimate. Travellers from Saudi Arabia usually need to spread their spending across flights, accommodation, transport, food, activities and unexpected fees. In this guide we give practical figures in Saudi riyals and US dollars, with an example of a full week in Moscow and St Petersburg. The aim is for you to know the minimum and average costs before paying, then choose what suits you with no financial surprises while travelling.

Cost of tourism in Russia: basic price ranges before booking

Return flights from Riyadh to Moscow usually cost between 1,400 and 2,800 riyals per person ($373-746) in normal seasons, and may rise to 3,200 riyals ($853) at peak times. Accommodation in Moscow usually costs between 260 and 620 riyals a night ($69-165), depending on location and rating. In St Petersburg , a night usually costs between 220 and 540 riyals ($59-144). These figures give a clear baseline before you compare any offers. Local transport by metro and bus for a light day out usually costs between 20 and 55 riyals ($5-15). Heavy use of private cars or ride-hailing apps may reach 95-180 riyals per day ($25-48). Food for one person on a mid-range budget costs between 85 and 170 riyals per day ($23-45). Always add a contingency of 10-15% on top of the total budget.

A practical 7-day budget: Moscow 4 days + St Petersburg 3 days

Mid-range solo example: flights 1900 riyals ($506), 7 nights’ accommodation at an average of 360 riyals = 2520 riyals ($672), high-speed train between the two cities 260 riyals ($69), local transport 280 riyals ($75), food 770 riyals ($205), activities and tickets 620 riyals ($165). The approximate total is 6,350 riyals ($1,692) before the contingency. Mid-range example for a family of 3: flights 5,700 riyals ($1,520), 7 nights in a serviced apartment 3,500 riyals ($933), local and intercity transport 1,450 riyals ($386), food 2,200 riyals ($586), activities 1,500 riyals ($400). The total is 14,350 riyals ($3,825), and it is advisable to add 1,500 riyals ($400) as a reserve.

Hidden costs that push the bill up quickly

The items that most often surprise travellers: excess baggage fees, exchange-rate differences on cards, night-time airport transfers, and cancellation or change fees. In some cases these can add 500-1,200 riyals ($133-320) to the trip without you noticing early on. So compare the final price after all the extras, not just the headline base price. Before accepting any offer, check the cancellation policy, local taxes, apartment cleaning fees and check-in times. A late arrival may mean paying for an extra night or a more expensive transfer. An accurate arrival schedule limits these losses and makes your financial planning more realistic.

How to cut the budget without sacrificing the quality of the trip

Choose accommodation close to a major metro station; this cuts transport costs and saves time every day. Book only the paid activities you do not want to miss, and leave the remaining days for a mix of self-guided walks and free sites. This way, entertainment costs usually fall by 20-30% while the experience stays good. Separate the flight decision from the accommodation decision, then link them once the schedule is set. This stops you accepting an unsuitable package just because one item is cheap. If you are working with a travel company, ask for a written breakdown that clearly lists what is and is not included.

Checklist before final payment

  1. Confirm the final flight price including baggage.
  2. Check the accommodation’s location on the map, not just in photos.
  3. Work out the airport-to-accommodation transfer based on your actual arrival time.
  4.  Add a contingency of at least 10%.
  5. Save all bookings in one file.
Once these steps are done, the cost of tourism in Russia becomes a figure you can control rather than an estimate that changes every day. This raises the quality of the trip from the outset, because the key decisions are settled financially before you travel.

Conclusion

The most important rule is that the cost of tourism in Russia should be calculated as clear line items, not as one overall sum. When you know the ranges for flights, accommodation, transport and food in dollars and riyals, you can make a more accurate booking decision and avoid surprises. Use the one-week example as an initial reference, then adjust the figures according to the season and the number of travellers. That way, the plan turns from a theoretical estimate into a practical working budget.

Frequently asked questions

What is the average budget for a week in Russia?

It varies with the season and type of accommodation, but good planning starts with a clear breakdown into flights, accommodation, transport, food and activities rather than one vague overall figure.

Which item pushes the cost up fastest?

Mostly flights and accommodation in central locations. Savings on these two items show up more directly in the total budget than savings on smaller items.

How do I avoid hidden expenses?

Compare the final price after baggage, taxes and payment fees, and set aside a small daily contingency so you are not caught out by unplanned expenses during the trip.
